title_candidates: Clean a photo before you share it
Photo Scrubber checks faces and metadata locally
summary: Photo Scrubber helps you review faces, cover visible identifiers, and remove embedded metadata in your browser before sharing a copy.

primary_source.title: Photo Scrubber — local face blur & metadata removal
primary_source.author: Simon Willison
key_facts: Photo Scrubber is an experimental browser tool for obscuring faces and stripping metadata before a photo is shared.
The tool processes photos locally and exports a new file without overwriting the original.
Automatic face detection scans the full image and overlapping crops, with an optional denser pass for smaller faces.
Users can adjust detections, draw boxes over missed details, and choose blur or a solid cover.
The tool accepts JPEG, PNG, and WebP files up to 75 MB; HEIC, RAW, SVG, animated PNG, and animated WebP are unsupported.
Export rebuilds the image from pixels and checks the JPEG or PNG structure so original EXIF, XMP, IPTC, comments, and thumbnails are not retained.
Automatic detection can miss small, turned, obscured, or difficult faces, while clothing, tattoos, text, and backgrounds can still identify a person.
The page reports no analytics, uploads, or persistent photo storage, but it loads pinned detector files from a CDN; high-risk users should audit and self-host the tool instead.

quote_candidates.text: Local processing. A new file, not an overwrite.
Blur is not guaranteed anonymity; use solid cover for stronger removal inside a region.

supporting_sources.title: Photo Scrubber — local face blur & metadata removal
key_facts: The live tool presents a three-stage workflow: choose a photo, review and adjust regions, then prepare and verify a clean copy.
Its interface warns that automatic detection can miss faces and that blur does not guarantee anonymity.
The tool checks the output for a restricted JPEG or PNG structure before enabling the download.

supporting_sources.title: Add Photo Scrubber tool
key_facts: The official source commit records the single-file implementation used for local face covering and metadata removal.

prerequisites: A modern browser with JavaScript enabled and an internet connection
A non-sensitive JPEG, PNG, or WebP test image no larger than 75 MB

steps.instruction: Open [Photo Scrubber](https://tools.simonwillison.net/photo-scrubber), then choose, drag, or paste a non-sensitive test photo. Confirm the review screen appears; your original file remains unchanged.
Turn on Show boxes and use Hold to compare while checking every face. If people are distant, run Find smaller faces and expect both extra detections and possible misses.
Use Draw region to cover every missed face plus identifying text, tattoos, badges, or background details. Choose Solid cover when anonymity matters because blur can retain recognizable detail.
Confirm that you reviewed the whole photo, choose the output format and dimensions, then select Prepare & verify image. Wait for Clean copy ready · metadata checked.

Download the clean image and inspect it at full size before sharing. Stop if any visible clue remains; for protests, abuse reports, or other high-risk images, use an audited or self-hosted workflow instead.
